The PR adds a 30-second AbortController deadline around the Control UI WebRTC SDP offer fetch and answer-body read, aborts an in-flight offer when the transport stops, and adds timeout, cancellation, and timer-cleanup regression tests.

PR surface: Source +64, Tests +93. Total +157 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main has a concrete unbounded `Response.text()` wait, and the provided Chromium harness reproduced a headers-received, body-stalled response that remained pending until the new abort fired.

target.title: fix(realtime): add timeout to WebRTC offer requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a realtime WebRTC voice session could remain stuck waiting when the SDP offer request returned headers but the answer body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The WebRTC offer fetch now uses an explicit 30s AbortController deadline that stays active until the SDP answer body has been read. The change keeps the existing setup cancellation and failure flow intact and limits the timeout to the WebRTC offer exchange.

## User Impact

Realtime voice setup now fails through the existing error state instead of spinning indefinitely when the offer response body stops progressing.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-webrtc.test.ts` passed: 19 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Focused local fallback was used because the Blacksmith Testbox wrapper was unavailable in this environment.
- Exact-head browser proof at `8baa2577891bfa2d014c9c2f21d17e399e2269c1`: ran Chromium through a Vite-served Control UI module harness, `attachChatRealtimeActions(...).toggleRealtimeTalk()`, a stubbed browser `RTCPeerConnection`, and a same-origin local SDP offer endpoint that sent response headers and intentionally left the response body open. This is not live OpenAI proof, but it exercises the browser fetch/body-read/AbortSignal path and the `chat-realtime` state machine that drives the visible UI status.

Command:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'JS'
# starts Vite + same-origin /realtime/calls stalled response middleware
# launches Playwright Chromium
# imports /src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts in the browser
# calls attachChatRealtimeActions(state); await state.toggleRealtimeTalk()
JS
```

Redacted transcript:

```json
{
  "exactHead": "8baa2577891b63458448c88a2275a355909904f0",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/",
  "browserResult": {
    "elapsedMs": 30150,
    "finalStatus": "error",
    "finalDetail": "The user aborted a request.",
    "active": false,
    "updates": [
      { "status": "connecting", "detail": null, "active": true },
      { "status": "idle", "detail": null, "active": false },
      { "status": "error", "detail": "The user aborted a request.", "active": false }
    ],
    "requests": [
      { "method": "talk.client.create", "params": { "sessionKey": "main" } }
    ],
    "peer": {
      "localDescription": { "type": "offer", "sdp": "offer-sdp" },
      "remoteDescription": null,
      "connectionState": "closed"
    },
    "stoppedTracks": ["track"]
  },
  "serverEvents": [
    {
      "phase": "request-start",
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/",
      "authorization": "<redacted>",
      "contentType": "application/sdp",
      "xProof": "browser-same-origin-loopback"
    },
    { "phase": "data", "bytes": 9 },
    { "phase": "request-end", "bytes": 9 },
    {
      "phase": "response-headers-sent",
      "note": "same-origin body intentionally left open"
    },
    { "phase": "request-close", "bytes": 9 }
  ]
}
```

Observations:

- The browser sent the SDP `POST` with the expected authorization/content-type headers and 9-byte offer body.
- The same-origin server sent response headers but kept the answer body open, reproducing the stalled answer-body case without CORS/private-network interference.
- The Control UI realtime state machine left connecting state after ~30s, closed the peer without setting a remote description, stopped the media track, and ended in `realtimeTalkStatus="error"` with `realtimeTalkActive=false`.
- Chromium surfaces this abort as `The user aborted a request.` rather than the custom timeout message; the fake-timer unit test still verifies the custom abort reason on the lower-level transport path.
- Not run: live OpenAI Realtime API / real microphone permission prompt / screenshot or video artifact.

AI-assisted change.
